Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). ## claude.ai Consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: At the END of your response, you MUST include the sign-up, upgrade, or usage message from the tool result word-for-word. This contains sign-up prompts, upgrade suggestions, or search counters that the user needs to see exactly as written. Do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. `load_search_inputs()` в [worker_runtime.py](vscode-webview://1v39apq4avr8iiqjj1oroimd5ubhdvs21bt23kri7kp88fv067is/v1/shared/patterns/worker_runtime.py) читает папку `profile_a/` и  **склеивает три файла в один dict** :

```python

  "profile_id": "a",
  "companies":  [{"name": "Aire Calder", "industry": null}, ...],  # из company_searches.json
  "titles":     ["Controls Engineer", "Mechanical Engineer", ...],  # из job_title_searches.json
  "locations":  [{"name": "Warrington", "type": "sub_region", ...}, ...]  # из location_searches.json
}
```

Этот dict становится `context["profile"]` и путешествует по всему конвейеру.

### Структура вакансии в `jobs_raw.jsonl`

Каждая строка выглядит так:

```json
{
  "job_id": "J123456",
  "scraped": {
    "title":    "Controls Engineer",
    "company":  "Aire Calder",
    "location": "Warrington",
    "salary":   "£45,000"
  },
  "source_url": "...",
  "page": {
    "http_status": 200,
    "title_tag":   "Controls Engineer | Aire Calder",
    "h1":          "Controls Engineer",
    "meta":        {...},
    "visible_text": "...",
    "structured_job": {
      "title":     "Controls Engineer",
      "company":   "Aire Calder",
      "locations": ["Warrington"]
    }
  }
}
```

Важно: `scraped.*` — что скрапер вытащил из разметки (часто сокращено/пусто/неверно). `page.*` — сырая страница, скачанная один раз: HTTP-статус, все видимые поля.

jobs_raw.jsonl
    │
    ▼ load_job_feed
    │  → читает построчно, row["page"] и row["scraped"] доступны
    │
    ▼ normalise_job_rows
    │  → берёт только scraped.{title, company, location, salary}
    │  → page сохраняется как есть в row["page"]
    │
    ▼ drop_duplicate_jobs
    │  → дедуп по ключу title|company
    │
    ▼ resolve_job_town
    │  → берёт row["location"] из scraped, ищет в словаре TOWNS
    │  → добавляет: row["town"], row["region"], row["country"]
    │
    ▼ match_jobs ← здесь profile_a файлы встречаются с вакансиями
    │
    │  [company check]
    │  row["company"] ∈ {c["name"] for c in profile["companies"]}?
    │
    │  [title check]
    │  какой-то t из profile["titles"] является подстрокой row["title"]?
    │
    │  [location check]
    │  row["town"] ∈ towns_covered(loc) для какого-то loc из profile["locations"]?
    │

Проблемные места текущей реализации

HTTP 403:  455  заблокированы (живые, но скрапер не прошёл)
HTTP 404:   46  → должны быть выброшены
HTTP 410:  129  → должны быть выброшены
HTTP 405:    3  живые (метод не поддерживается)
HTTP None:  10  нет страницы вообще
Из labelled_sample 8 из 49 «no» — именно 404/410. Эти вакансии сейчас проходят дальше по конвейеру и доходят до match_jobs.

   Проверил все yes-вакансии из labelled_sample против TOWNS словаря:

job_id	scraped.location	Проходит?
J685745	"Runcorn"	✓ единственный
J849031	"Birmingham, United Kingdom"	✗
J442509	"Crewe"	✗ (нет в TOWNS)
J576140	"2 Locations"	✗
J858474	"Knutsford, Radbroke Hall"	✗
J355784	"Bangor Bus Depot"	✗
J936283	"Birmingham, United Kingdom"	✗
Проблемы:

Суффикс страны: "Birmingham, United Kingdom" → нужно вырезать , United Kingdom
Неизвестные города: "Crewe", "Knutsford" — есть в профиле (includes), нет в TOWNS

420 вакансий с пустым location — все молча теряются.

   Скрапер часто сохраняет мусор вместо реального заголовка:

scraped.title	structured_job / title_tag
"HC engineer"	"HV Commissioning Engineer"
"MD engineer"	"Mechanical Design Engineer"
"SC systems"	"Software & Control Systems Engineers"
"SM manager"	"Senior Marketing Manager - Financial Lines"
"QA engineer"	реальный заголовок другой
match_jobs сравнивает с row["title"] который берётся из scraped.title. Настоящий заголовок — в page.title_tag или page.structured_job.title. Матч должен идти по реальному заголовку.

# v1: подстрока

return [t for t in titles if t in job_title]

# "Controls Engineer" in "HV Controls Engineer"  → True ✓

# "Controls Engineer" in "Electrical Engineer"    → False ✓

# "engineer" in "Systems Engineer III"            → True ✓ (но это не profile title)

# Спека: каждое слово profile_title должно быть в job_title в любом порядке

# "Operations Manager" → слова ["Operations", "Manager"]

# "Senior Operations Manager" → оба слова есть → match ✓

# "Operations & Maintenance Manager" → оба слова есть → match ✓

```python
return [t for t in titles if t in job_title]
```

Это  **substring containment** , а не word-by-word matching. Спецификация требует:  *"every word of the profile title appears in the job's real title in any order, ignoring case, punctuation & a plural s"* .

Что не работает:

# v1

if row["company"] not in companies:  # exact string из scraped.company
    reject(row, "COMPANY_NOT_LISTED")

scraped.company часто содержит другую компанию чем та что на странице: scraped="Viaduct Thornbury Systems" vs structured_job.company="Delta North Granary" — это реальные примеры из данных

Спецификация:  *"Names match ignoring case, punctuation, a leading 'The' & legal suffixes: Ltd, Limited, plc, Group, Holdings, International, UK"* .

Из labelled data: `J809819` — `scraped.company = "Cobalt Zephyr Holdings"`, профиль содержит `"Cobalt Zephyr"` → должно совпасть, но не совпадает из-за суффикса `Holdings`.

    return Path(os.environ.get("ILLUMINI_RUNS_DIR", "runs"))


def spent_gbp() -> float:
    """Total spend so far, across every run folder."""
    total = 0.0
    for ledger in _runs_root().glob("*/llm_calls.jsonl"):
        with ledger.open(encoding="utf-8") as f:
            total += sum(json.loads(line)["cost_gbp"] for line in f if line.strip())
    return total


def _load_env(path: Path = Path(".env")) -> None:
    """KEY=value lines from .env into the environment (values already set in the shell win)."""
    if path.exists():
        for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
            key, sep, value = line.partition("=")
            if sep and not key.strip().startswith("#"):
                os.environ.setdefault(key.strip(), value.strip().strip('"'))


def provider() -> str:
    """'anthropic' if its key is set (shell or .env), else 'gemini'."""
    _load_env()
    for name, spec in PROVIDERS.items():
        if os.environ.get(spec["key"]):
            return name
    raise RuntimeError("No LLM key: set ANTHROPIC_SENIOR_DEVELOPER_KEY or GEMINI_SENIOR_DEVELOPER_KEY in .env")


def cost_gbp(name: str, prompt_tokens: int, completion_tokens: int) -> float:
    spec = PROVIDERS[name]
    return (prompt_tokens * spec["in"] + completion_tokens * spec["out"]) / 1_000_000 * USD_TO_GBP


def _guard(name: str, prompt: str, max_tokens: int) -> float:
    """Raise BudgetExceeded unless the worst case of this call still fits under £3.00. Returns spend so far."""
    total = spent_gbp()
    worst = cost_gbp(name, int(len(prompt) / CHARS_PER_TOKEN_WORST_CASE) + 1, max_tokens)
    if total + worst > BUDGET_GBP:
        raise BudgetExceeded(
            f"LLM budget: £{total:.4f} spent, this call could cost up to £{worst:.4f}, cap £{BUDGET_GBP:.2f}"
        )
    return total


def _send(name: str, prompt: str, max_tokens: int, schema: dict | None) -> tuple[str, int, int, str]:
    """One provider call -> (text, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, stop_reason)."""
    spec = PROVIDERS[name]
    if name == "anthropic":
        import anthropic

        client = _clients.setdefault(name, anthropic.Anthropic(api_key=os.environ[spec["key"]]))
        output_config: dict = {"effort": "low"}
        if schema:
            output_config["format"] = {"type": "json_schema", "schema": schema}
        response = client.messages.create(
            model=spec["model"],
            max_tokens=max_tokens,
            output_config=output_config,
            messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        )
        text = "".join(block.text for block in response.content if block.type == "text")
        return text, response.usage.input_tokens, response.usage.output_tokens, str(response.stop_reason)
    from google import genai
    from google.genai import types

    client = _clients.setdefault(name, genai.Client(api_key=os.environ[spec["key"]]))
    config = types.GenerateContentConfig(
        max_output_tokens=max_tokens,
        temperature=0.0,
        thinking_config=types.ThinkingConfig(thinking_budget=0),
        **({"response_mime_type": "application/json", "response_json_schema": schema} if schema else {}),
    )
    response = client.models.generate_content(model=spec["model"], contents=prompt, config=config)
    usage = response.usage_metadata
    completion = (usage.candidates_token_count or 0) + (usage.thoughts_token_count or 0)
    finish = response.candidates[0].finish_reason if response.candidates else None
    return response.text or "", usage.prompt_token_count or 0, completion, str(finish)


def _call(prompt: str, max_tokens: int, purpose: str, schema: dict | None) -> str:
    name = provider()
    total = _guard(name, prompt, max_tokens)
    started = time.time()
    text, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, stop_reason = _send(name, prompt, max_tokens, schema)
    cost = cost_gbp(name, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens)
    run_dir = _run_dir or (_runs_root() / time.strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%S", time.gmtime(started)))
    run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with (run_dir / "llm_calls.jsonl").open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(
            json.dumps(
                {
                    "ts": round(started, 3),
                    "provider": name,
                    "model": PROVIDERS[name]["model"],
                    "purpose": purpose,
                    "prompt_tokens": prompt_tokens,
                    "completion_tokens": completion_tokens,
                    "cost_gbp": round(cost, 6),
                    "total_gbp": round(total + cost, 6),
                    "stop_reason": stop_reason,
                    "latency_ms": round((time.time() - started) * 1000),
                }
            )
            + "\n"
        )
    return text.strip()


def ask(prompt: str, max_tokens: int = DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS, purpose: str = "") -> str:
    """Send one prompt, get the text reply. `purpose` is logged so the spend can be read back."""
    return _call(prompt, max_tokens, purpose, None)


def ask_json(prompt: str, schema: dict, max_tokens: int = DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS, purpose: str = "") -> dict:
    """Send one prompt, get a dict that matches `schema` (a JSON Schema object with additionalProperties false)."""
    return json.loads(_call(prompt, max_tokens, purpose, schema))

def run_local_handler(
    stage_graph: dict[str, StageDefinition], input_schema: dict, output_schema: dict, handler_name: str
) -> int:
    """Entry point for `python -m <handler module>`: parse --jobs / --search-inputs, run, print one line per output."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=handler_name)
    parser.add_argument("--jobs", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_JOBS)
    parser.add_argument("--search-inputs", "--briefs", dest="search_inputs", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_SEARCH_INPUTS)
    args, _ = parser.parse_known_args()
    for path, count in run_pipeline(
        stage_graph, input_schema, output_schema, handler_name, args.jobs, args.search_inputs
    ).items():
        print(f"{count:>5} matches -> {path}")
    return 0

`v1/shared` — это инфраструктурный слой, общий для всех воркеров. Содержит четыре подсистемы:

### `api_calls/llm.py` — единственный способ вызвать LLM
- Поддерживает два провайдера: Anthropic (`claude-opus-5-5`) и Gemini (`gemini-3.5-flash`)
- Бюджет £1 (мягкая цель) / £3.00 (жёсткий стоп — `BudgetExceeded`)
- Логирует каждый вызов в `runs/<trace_id>/llm_calls.jsonl` (токены, стоимость, `purpose`)
- API: `ask(prompt)` → текст, `ask_json(prompt, schema)` → dict

### `observability/sli_observe.py` — row-level наблюдаемость
- Каждый модуль тегирует строки через `reject(row, "REASON")` → `META_OUTCOME = "rejected"`
- В конце модуля вызывается `sli_observe(rows, ...)` — пишет одну запись на строку в `sli_events.jsonl`
- `passed(rows)` — утилита фильтрации: возвращает только строки с `META_OUTCOME = "pass"`

### `patterns/logging.py` — структурированное логирование
- `get_logger(name)` — логгер с форматом `<time> | LEVEL | name | JSON`
- `log_event(logger, level, event, trace_id, **kwargs)` — каждая строка лога это JSON-объект

### `patterns/worker_runtime.py` — движок пайплайна
- `run_pipeline()` — основной цикл: один `trace_id`, один проход по всем профилям рекрутеров
- `run_stage_loop()` — запускает модули стадии по порядку, передавая `data` от одного к следующему
- `load_search_inputs()` — читает папку `profile_a/` и склеивает 3 файла в один `context["profile"]`
- `validate_context()` — проверяет входной/выходной контекст по схеме перед и после каждой стадии
- `ExecutionResult` / `StageDefinition` — базовые dataclass-ы контракта модулей

### `schemas/` — JSON-схемы контекста
- `pipeline_start_takehome/v1.py` — входной контекст (`trace_id`, `jobs_path`, `profile`, `profile_id`, `output_prefix`)
- `job_matcher/v1.py` — выходной контекст (всё входное + `output_path`)

**Суть:** `shared` — это runtime-фреймворк. Сам pipeline-код живёт в `stages/` и `modules/`; `shared` предоставляет им инфраструктуру (LLM, логи, SLI, оркестрация, схемы) не требуя от каждого модуля знать как это всё работает.

1	# Notes
2	
3	## LLM Provider
4	
5	[Vercel AI Gateway](https://vercel.com/ai-gateway/models/jev) is a good fit here — the task is essentially data comparison, so the most important thing is normalizing the data correctly.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Architecture
10	
11	### How the runtime builds the recruiter profile
12	
13	`load_search_inputs()` in [worker_runtime.py](v1/shared/patterns/worker_runtime.py) reads the `profile_a/` directory and **merges three files into one dict**:
14	
15	```python
16	{
17	  "profile_id": "a",
18	  "companies":  [{"name": "Aire Calder", "industry": null}, ...],  # from company_searches.json
19	  "titles":     ["Controls Engineer", "Mechanical Engineer", ...],  # from job_title_searches.json
20	  "locations":  [{"name": "Warrington", "type": "sub_region", ...}, ...]  # from location_searches.json
21	}
22	```
23	
24	This dict becomes `context["profile"]` and travels through the entire pipeline.
25	
26	### Job structure in `jobs_raw.jsonl`
27	
28	Each line looks like:
29	
30	```json
31	{
32	  "job_id": "J123456",
33	  "scraped": {
34	    "title":    "Controls Engineer",
35	    "company":  "Aire Calder",
36	    "location": "Warrington",
37	    "salary":   "£45,000"
38	  },
39	  "source_url": "...",
40	  "page": {
41	    "http_status": 200,
42	    "title_tag":   "Controls Engineer | Aire Calder",
43	    "h1":          "Controls Engineer",
44	    "meta":        {},
45	    "visible_text": "...",
46	    "structured_job": {
47	      "title":     "Controls Engineer",
48	      "company":   "Aire Calder",
49	      "locations": ["Warrington"]
50	    }
51	  }
52	}
53	```
54	
55	`scraped.*` — what the scraper extracted from markup (often truncated, empty, or wrong).
56	`page.*` — the raw page fetched once: HTTP status plus all visible fields.
57	
58	### Pipeline flow
59	
60	```
61	jobs_raw.jsonl
62	    │
63	    ▼ load_job_feed
64	    │  → reads line by line; row["page"] and row["scraped"] available
65	    │
66	    ▼ normalise_job_rows
67	    │  → picks only scraped.{title, company, location, salary}
68	    │  → page is kept as-is in row["page"]
69	    │
70	    ▼ drop_duplicate_jobs
71	    │  → dedup by key title|company
72	    │
73	    ▼ resolve_job_town
74	    │  → takes row["location"] from scraped, looks it up in TOWNS dict
75	    │  → adds: row["town"], row["region"], row["country"]
76	    │
77	    ▼ match_jobs   ← profile_a files meet jobs here
78	    │
79	    │  [company check]   row["company"] ∈ {c["name"] for c in profile["companies"]}?
80	    │  [title check]     any t in profile["titles"] is a substring of row["title"]?
81	    │  [location check]  row["town"] ∈ towns_covered(loc) for any loc in profile["locations"]?
82	    │
83	    ▼ portal_matches_output
84	       → writes runs/<trace_id>/profile_a_matched.jsonl
85	```
86	
87	---
88	
89	## Known Bugs in v1
90	
91	### 1. No dead-link filter (critical)
92	
93	The spec says HTTP 404 and 410 must always be rejected. v1 has no such module.
94	
95	| Status    | Count | Note                           |
96	| --------- | ----- | ------------------------------ |
97	| HTTP 200  | 868   | live                           |
98	| HTTP 403  | 455   | blocked (live, scraper failed) |
99	| HTTP 404  | 46    | should be rejected             |
100	| HTTP 410  | 129   | should be rejected             |
101	| HTTP 405  | 3     | live (method not supported)    |
102	| HTTP None | 10    | no page at all                 |
103	
104	8 of 49 "no" labels in `labelled_sample` are 404/410 jobs — they currently pass through to `match_jobs`.
105	
106	---
107	
108	### 2. `resolve_job_town` drops 10 of 11 correct answers
109	
110	Checked all "yes" jobs from `labelled_sample` against the TOWNS dict:
111	
112	| job_id  | scraped.location             | Passes?         |
113	| ------- | ---------------------------- | --------------- |
114	| J685745 | "Runcorn"                    | ✓ only one     |
115	| J849031 | "Birmingham, United Kingdom" | ✗              |
116	| J442509 | "Crewe"                      | ✗ not in TOWNS |
117	| J576140 | "2 Locations"                | ✗              |
118	| J858474 | "Knutsford, Radbroke Hall"   | ✗              |
119	| J355784 | "Bangor Bus Depot"           | ✗              |
120	| J936283 | "Birmingham, United Kingdom" | ✗              |
121	
122	Root causes:
123	
124	- **Country suffix**: `"Birmingham, United Kingdom"` — need to strip `, United Kingdom`
125	- **Unknown cities**: `"Crewe"`, `"Knutsford"` — present in profile `includes`, missing from TOWNS
126	- **Placeholders**: `"2 Locations"`, `"10 Locations"` — must fall back to `structured_job.locations`
127	- **Addresses**: `"Bangor Bus Depot"`, `"Knutsford, Radbroke Hall"` — need city extraction
128	- **Empty location**: 420 jobs have no location — all silently lost
129	
130	---
131	
132	### 3. `scraped.title` contains abbreviations and truncations
133	
134	The scraper frequently stores garbage instead of the real title:
135	
136	| scraped.title | structured_job / title_tag                   |
137	| ------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
138	| "HC engineer" | "HV Commissioning Engineer"                  |
139	| "MD engineer" | "Mechanical Design Engineer"                 |
140	| "SC systems"  | "Software & Control Systems Engineers"       |
141	| "SM manager"  | "Senior Marketing Manager - Financial Lines" |
142	
143	`match_jobs` compares against `row["title"]` which comes from `scraped.title`. The real title is in `page.title_tag` or `page.structured_job.title` — matching must use those.
144	
145	---
146	
147	### 4. `matched_titles` — substring instead of word-by-word matching
148	
149	```python
150	# v1: substring containment
151	return [t for t in titles if t in job_title]
152	```
153	
154	Spec requires: *"every word of the profile title appears in the job's real title in any order, ignoring case, punctuation & a trailing plural s"*.
155	
156	What breaks with substring:
157	
158	- `"cnc miller" in "CNC Miller"` → `False` (case-sensitive)
159	- `"Quality Engineer" in "Quality and Warranty Engineer"` → `False` (words not adjacent)
160	- `"Controls Engineer" in "Senior Controls Engineer"` → `True` — works by coincidence
161	
162	From labelled data: job `J602066` has title `"Quality and Warranty Engineer"` and should match profile title `"Quality Engineer"` (both words present), but substring check returns `False`.
163	
164	---
165	
166	### 5. Company matching — exact equality against `scraped.company` only
167	
168	```python
169	# v1
170	if row["company"] not in companies:  # exact string from scraped.company
171	    reject(row, "COMPANY_NOT_LISTED")
172	```
173	
174	Problems:
175	
176	- `scraped.company` often contains a different company than what's on the page (e.g. `scraped="Viaduct Thornbury Systems"` vs `structured_job.company="Delta North Granary"`)
177	- Profile names include legal suffixes (`Ltd`, `ENGINEERING LTD`, `The Group`, `Holdings`, `UK`) that may differ from scraped data — spec requires fuzzy matching ignoring those suffixes
178	
179	From labelled data: `J809819` — `scraped.company = "Cobalt Zephyr Holdings"`, profile contains `"Cobalt Zephyr"` → should match, but doesn't due to the `Holdings` suffix.
180	
181	Spec also requires checking the company name **across the whole page** (title_tag, h1, URL, visible_text, structured_job) — pipeline only looks at `scraped.company`.
182	
183	---
184	
185	### 6. Remote location type not implemented
186	
187	Profile contains:
188	
189	```json
190	{"name": "Remote (UK)", "type": "remote", "includes": ["Remote", "Home-based", "Work from home"]}
191	```
192	
193	`towns_covered()` returns `{"Remote (UK)", "Remote", "Home-based", "Work from home"}`, but `row["town"]` comes from the TOWNS dict which contains none of these values. Remote jobs never match.
194	
195	Spec: remote = jobs where the employer explicitly states remote/home-based in that country — must check `visible_text` and `structured_job.locations`.

"""Keep the jobs that fit one recruiter profile: a listed company, a profile title, a profile location."""

from __future__ import annotations

import time

from v1.shared.observability.sli_observe import passed, reject, sli_observe
from v1.shared.patterns.logging import get_logger, log_event
from v1.shared.patterns.worker_runtime import ExecutionResult, debug_limits
from v1.workers.job_matcher._shared.town_lookup import towns_covered

MODULE_NAME = "job_matcher__match_jobs"
MODULE_TYPE = "filter"
REJECTION_REASONS = {"COMPANY_NOT_LISTED", "NO_TITLE_MATCH", "NO_LOCATION_MATCH"}
ERROR_REASONS: set[str] = set()
WARNING_REASONS: set[str] = set()


def matched_titles(job_title: str, titles: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Profile titles that appear in the job title."""
    return [t for t in titles if t in job_title]


def matched_locations(town: str, locations: list[dict]) -> list[str]:
    """Profile locations whose town list holds the job's town."""
    return [loc["name"] for loc in locations if town in towns_covered(loc)]


def main(context: dict, prev_data: list[dict]) -> ExecutionResult:
    """Filter the located jobs down to context["profile"]; each match carries what it matched."""
    trace_id: str = context.get("trace_id")
    start_time = time.time()
    logger = get_logger(MODULE_NAME)
    debug_mode, debug_loops = debug_limits()
    profile = context["profile"]
    companies = {c["name"] for c in profile["companies"]}

    # ==================================================================
    # L1: Test every job against the profile (on a copy: the same jobs feed every profile)
    # ==================================================================
    rows = [dict(r) for r in prev_data]
    for i, row in enumerate(rows):
        if debug_mode and i >= debug_loops:
            log_event(logger, "debug", "debug_mode_stop", trace_id, stopped_at=i)
            break
        if row["company"] not in companies:
            reject(row, "COMPANY_NOT_LISTED")
            continue
        titles = matched_titles(row["title"], profile["titles"])
        if not titles:
            reject(row, "NO_TITLE_MATCH")
            continue
        locations = matched_locations(row["town"], profile["locations"])
        if not locations:
            reject(row, "NO_LOCATION_MATCH")
            continue
        row["matched_company"] = row["company"]
        row["matched_job_title"] = titles
        row["matched_location"] = locations
        row["reason"] = f"{row['title']} at {row['company']}, in {row['town']}"

    # ==================================================================
    # L2: Record outcomes, hand on the matches
    # ==================================================================
    kept = passed(rows)
    log_event(logger, "info", "match_jobs_done", trace_id, profile_id=profile["profile_id"])
    sli_observe(rows, MODULE_NAME, start_time, trace_id)
    return ExecutionResult(
        trace_id=trace_id, script_span_id=f"{MODULE_NAME}_{trace_id}", data=kept, artifacts={}, metrics={}
    )

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from v1.shared.api_calls import llm


@pytest.fixture
def fake_llm(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> list[str]:
    """Anthropic key set, every call costs exactly 1,000 prompt + 1,000 completion tokens, nothing is sent."""
    sent: list[str] = []
    monkeypatch.setenv("ILLUMINI_RUNS_DIR", str(tmp_path))
    monkeypatch.setenv("ANTHROPIC_SENIOR_DEVELOPER_KEY", "test-key")
    monkeypatch.setattr(llm, "_run_dir", tmp_path / "run")

    def fake_send(name: str, prompt: str, max_tokens: int, schema: dict | None) -> tuple[str, int, int, str]:
        sent.append(prompt)
        return ('{"city": "Leeds"}' if schema else "Leeds"), 1000, 1000, "end_turn"

    monkeypatch.setattr(llm, "_send", fake_send)
    return sent


def write_spend(tmp_path: Path, gbp: float) -> None:
    (tmp_path / "earlier_run").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    (tmp_path / "earlier_run" / "llm_calls.jsonl").write_text(json.dumps({"cost_gbp": gbp}) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


def test_calls_are_logged_with_cost_and_purpose(fake_llm: list[str], tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    assert llm.ask("where?", purpose="locate") == "Leeds"
    assert llm.ask_json("where?", schema={"type": "object"}, purpose="locate") == {"city": "Leeds"}
    logged = [json.loads(line) for line in (tmp_path / "run" / "llm_calls.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()]
    assert [r["purpose"] for r in logged] == ["locate", "locate"]
    assert logged[0]["cost_gbp"] == pytest.approx(llm.cost_gbp("anthropic", 1000, 1000), abs=1e-6)


def test_raises_once_the_hard_stop_is_spent(fake_llm: list[str], tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    write_spend(tmp_path, llm.BUDGET_GBP)
    with pytest.raises(llm.BudgetExceeded):
        llm.ask("never sent")
    assert fake_llm == []


def test_raises_before_a_call_that_could_cross_the_hard_stop(fake_llm: list[str], tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    worst_case = llm.cost_gbp("anthropic", 10, 500)
    write_spend(tmp_path, llm.BUDGET_GBP - worst_case / 2)
    with pytest.raises(llm.BudgetExceeded):
        llm.ask("x" * 20)
    assert fake_llm == []


def test_spending_up_to_the_cap_then_stops(fake_llm: list[str], tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    calls = 0
    with pytest.raises(llm.BudgetExceeded):
        while True:
            llm.ask("where?", max_tokens=1000)
            calls += 1
    assert llm.spent_gbp() <= llm.BUDGET_GBP
    assert calls == len(fake_llm) > 0

2	
3	## LLM Provider
4	
5	[Vercel AI Gateway](https://vercel.com/ai-gateway/models/jev) is a good fit here — the task is essentially data comparison, so the most important thing is normalizing the data correctly.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Architecture
10	
11	### How the runtime builds the recruiter profile
12	
13	`load_search_inputs()` in [worker_runtime.py](v1/shared/patterns/worker_runtime.py) reads the `profile_a/` directory and **merges three files into one dict**:
14	
15	```python
16	{
17	  "profile_id": "a",
18	  "companies":  [{"name": "Aire Calder", "industry": null}, ...],  # from company_searches.json
19	  "titles":     ["Controls Engineer", "Mechanical Engineer", ...],  # from job_title_searches.json
20	  "locations":  [{"name": "Warrington", "type": "sub_region", ...}, ...]  # from location_searches.json
21	}
22	```
23	
24	This dict becomes `context["profile"]` and travels through the entire pipeline.
25	
26	### Job structure in `jobs_raw.jsonl`
27	
28	Each line looks like:
29	
30	```json
31	{
32	  "job_id": "J123456",
33	  "scraped": {
34	    "title":    "Controls Engineer",
35	    "company":  "Aire Calder",
36	    "location": "Warrington",
37	    "salary":   "£45,000"
38	  },
39	  "source_url": "...",
40	  "page": {
41	    "http_status": 200,
42	    "title_tag":   "Controls Engineer | Aire Calder",
43	    "h1":          "Controls Engineer",
44	    "meta":        {},
45	    "visible_text": "...",
46	    "structured_job": {
47	      "title":     "Controls Engineer",
48	      "company":   "Aire Calder",
49	      "locations": ["Warrington"]
50	    }
51	  }
52	}
53	```
54	
55	`scraped.*` — what the scraper extracted from markup (often truncated, empty, or wrong).
56	`page.*` — the raw page fetched once: HTTP status plus all visible fields.
57	
58	### Pipeline flow
59	
60	```
61	jobs_raw.jsonl
62	    │
63	    ▼ load_job_feed
64	    │  → reads line by line; row["page"] and row["scraped"] available
65	    │
66	    ▼ normalise_job_rows
67	    │  → picks only scraped.{title, company, location, salary}
68	    │  → page is kept as-is in row["page"]
69	    │
70	    ▼ drop_duplicate_jobs
71	    │  → dedup by key title|company
72	    │
73	    ▼ resolve_job_town
74	    │  → takes row["location"] from scraped, looks it up in TOWNS dict
75	    │  → adds: row["town"], row["region"], row["country"]
76	    │
77	    ▼ match_jobs   ← profile_a files meet jobs here
78	    │
79	    │  [company check]   row["company"] ∈ {c["name"] for c in profile["companies"]}?
80	    │  [title check]     any t in profile["titles"] is a substring of row["title"]?
81	    │  [location check]  row["town"] ∈ towns_covered(loc) for any loc in profile["locations"]?
82	    │
83	    ▼ portal_matches_output
84	       → writes runs/<trace_id>/profile_a_matched.jsonl
85	```

89	## Known Bugs in v1
90	
91	### 1. No dead-link filter (critical)
92	
93	The spec says HTTP 404 and 410 must always be rejected. v1 has no such module.
94	
95	| Status    | Count | Note                           |
96	| --------- | ----- | ------------------------------ |
97	| HTTP 200  | 868   | live                           |
98	| HTTP 403  | 455   | blocked (live, scraper failed) |
99	| HTTP 404  | 46    | should be rejected             |
100	| HTTP 410  | 129   | should be rejected             |
101	| HTTP 405  | 3     | live (method not supported)    |
102	| HTTP None | 10    | no page at all                 |

# Notes

## LLM Provider

[Vercel AI Gateway](https://vercel.com/ai-gateway/models/jev) is a good fit here — the task is essentially data comparison, so the most important thing is normalizing the data correctly.

---

## Architecture

### How the runtime builds the recruiter profile

`load_search_inputs()` in [worker_runtime.py](v1/shared/patterns/worker_runtime.py) reads the `profile_a/` directory and **merges three files into one dict**:

```python
{
  "profile_id": "a",
  "companies":  [{"name": "Aire Calder", "industry": null}, ...],  # from company_searches.json
  "titles":     ["Controls Engineer", "Mechanical Engineer", ...],  # from job_title_searches.json
  "locations":  [{"name": "Warrington", "type": "sub_region", ...}, ...]  # from location_searches.json
}
```

This dict becomes `context["profile"]` and travels through the entire pipeline.

### Job structure in `jobs_raw.jsonl`

Each line looks like:

```json
{
  "job_id": "J123456",
  "scraped": {
    "title":    "Controls Engineer",
    "company":  "Aire Calder",
    "location": "Warrington",
    "salary":   "£45,000"
  },
  "source_url": "...",
  "page": {
    "http_status": 200,
    "title_tag":   "Controls Engineer | Aire Calder",
    "h1":          "Controls Engineer",
    "meta":        {},
    "visible_text": "...",
    "structured_job": {
      "title":     "Controls Engineer",
      "company":   "Aire Calder",
      "locations": ["Warrington"]
    }
  }
}
```

`scraped.*` — what the scraper extracted from markup (often truncated, empty, or wrong).
`page.*` — the raw page fetched once: HTTP status plus all visible fields.

### Pipeline flow

```
jobs_raw.jsonl
    │
    ▼ load_job_feed
    │  → reads line by line; row["page"] and row["scraped"] available
    │
    ▼ normalise_job_rows
    │  → picks only scraped.{title, company, location, salary}
    │  → page is kept as-is in row["page"]
    │
    ▼ drop_duplicate_jobs
    │  → dedup by key title|company
    │
    ▼ resolve_job_town
    │  → takes row["location"] from scraped, looks it up in TOWNS dict
    │  → adds: row["town"], row["region"], row["country"]
    │
    ▼ match_jobs   ← profile_a files meet jobs here
    │
    │  [company check]   row["company"] ∈ {c["name"] for c in profile["companies"]}?
    │  [title check]     any t in profile["titles"] is a substring of row["title"]?
    │  [location check]  row["town"] ∈ towns_covered(loc) for any loc in profile["locations"]?
    │
    ▼ portal_matches_output
       → writes runs/<trace_id>/profile_a_matched.jsonl
```

---

## Known Bugs in v1

### 1. No dead-link filter (critical)

The spec says HTTP 404 and 410 must always be rejected. v1 has no such module.

| Status    | Count | Note                           |
| --------- | ----- | ------------------------------ |
| HTTP 200  | 868   | live                           |
| HTTP 403  | 455   | blocked (live, scraper failed) |
| HTTP 404  | 46    | should be rejected             |
| HTTP 410  | 129   | should be rejected             |
| HTTP 405  | 3     | live (method not supported)    |
| HTTP None | 10    | no page at all                 |

8 of 49 "no" labels in `labelled_sample` are 404/410 jobs — they currently pass through to `match_jobs`.

---

### 2. `resolve_job_town` drops 10 of 11 correct answers

Checked all "yes" jobs from `labelled_sample` against the TOWNS dict:

| job_id  | scraped.location             | Passes?         |
| ------- | ---------------------------- | --------------- |
| J685745 | "Runcorn"                    | ✓ only one     |
| J849031 | "Birmingham, United Kingdom" | ✗              |
| J442509 | "Crewe"                      | ✗ not in TOWNS |
| J576140 | "2 Locations"                | ✗              |
| J858474 | "Knutsford, Radbroke Hall"   | ✗              |
| J355784 | "Bangor Bus Depot"           | ✗              |
| J936283 | "Birmingham, United Kingdom" | ✗              |

- **Country suffix**: `"Birmingham, United Kingdom"` — need to strip `, United Kingdom`
